full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts necessary for the disposal of this Civil Appeal are in a mutshell, that the predecessor of the respondents No.1(a)-1(g), Md Rafiquzzaman Bhuiyan as plaintiff filed the Other Class Suit No.201 of 1980 on 12-11-1980 for declaration of title over "Kha' schedule land and later on after amendment prayed for recovery of Khas possession by evicting the defendants No. 8-10 from the suit land as appended to the plaint stating, inter alia, that the father of plaintiff Md Rafiquzzaman Bhuiyan and the pro-forma defendants No.2-6, namely Alhaj Ali Azam purchased 0.22 acres of land by Kabala dated 10-2-1953 from Kailash Chandra Bhuiyan, Khetra Mohan Bhuiyan and Botu Keshar Bhuiyan in the Benami of pro-forma defendant No.7. Said Alhaj Ali Azam died leaving behind the plaintiff Md Rafiquzzaman Bhuiyan and the pro-forma defendants No.2-6 as sons and daughters. The plaintiff got the suit "Kha' schedule land by amicable partition with pro-forma defendants No. 2-6 and since the date of Kabala the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land. On 1240-1980 the plaintiff came to know that the suit land has been recorded in Khas Khatian in the name of the defendant No. l. The defendant No.1 is trying to lease out the suit land. By a subsequent amendment to the plaint the plaintiff further claimed that during the pendency of the suit the defendants No.8-10 forcibly entered into the suit land on 18-11-1980 and constructed a tin-shed structure although they were not entitled to enter into or construct any house in the suit land. 

 3. The government as defendant No.1 contested the said suit by filing written statement, contending, inter alia, that the suit land is government Khas land and is part of the Bazar namely Zamindar Hat. The said land has been recorded in Khas Khatian No.1 during SA and MRR operation, All the Bazars became khas land and were vested to the government from 1st Baishak 1368 BS as per The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the government has been leasing out the said Bazar since 1368 BS Accordingly during preparation of MRR Kkatian the same has been recorded as Hat in the name of the Government, The plaintiff never possessed the suit land and, as such, he has no right, title or interest over the suit land, hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. The suit land is being possessed by the defendant No. 7, who constructed a grocery shop thereon and subsequently applied for lease of the Suit land. 

 7. Mr Md Taherul Islam, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the appellant has taken us through the judgment and decree of the High Court Division dated 10-5-2006 passed in Civil Revision No.3151 of 1998, judgment and decree of trial Court as well as appellate Court, the other materials on record and contends that the High Court Division has committed illegality in totally misconceiving the case of the petitioner upon misreading and misconstruing the evidence and materials on record and thereby misdirected beyond the law and facts of the case in passing the erroneous discharging the Rule absolute occasioning serious miscarriage of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. The learned Counsel for the appellant contends next that the all the courts below failed to appreciate that the suit land is the land of Hat belonging to the government and the same is in possession of the government from a long time. Accordingly, the suit land was recorded in the name of the government in MRR and BS Khatian. The learned Counsel argues next that the government has been possessing the suit land through the defendant No.7, who constructed a grocery shop thereon and subsequently applied for taking lease of the suit land, but all the Courts below did not consider the said facts. The learned Counsel submits further that the appellate Court in its judgment mentioned that C-1, C-2 and D files of the original suit has been destroyed from the record room of the learned District Judge and the parties were directed to file documents including the copy of oral evidence, but the parties did not file any copy of oral evidence yet the appellate Court affirmed the judgment of trial Court and thereafter the High Court Division also upheld the judgment of appellate Court and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division is liable to be scraped. 

 12. Again, on plain reading of DS Khatian No.58 (Exhibit 3) it appears that the suit plot No.2141 was recorded in the name of the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff's father named Swarup Chandra Bhuiyan from whom the plaintiff's father purchased the suit land in benami of the defendant No.7. It also appears from the Exhibit-3 that the nature of the suit land had been described in DS Khatian as orchard'. Had the suit land been part of Hat then it should have been written to the same effect. The plaintiff claimed that he used to cut down the trees on the suit land from time to time and for the said reason the suit land was vacant land. PW 2 also stated in his deposition that the suit land was orchard. In the similar way, PW 3 deposed supporting the deposition of PWs 1 and 2 regarding the said assertion. It was argued on behalf of the defendant No.1 that the suit land being in close proximity to a Bazaar and said Bazaar had later on extended to the suit land. But the said claim of the defendant No.1 was not supported by the evidence on record. On the other hand, it is settled principle of law that mere recording of the suit land in the name of the defendant No.1 without proof of title does not devolve any ownership of the suit land upon the defendant No. l. In the light of the discussion made above, it is crystal clear that the plaintiff has title and possession of the suit land prior to dispossession on 18-11-1980.
